title: Cigarroa Presses Staff on Center for the Arts Contract at Monday Council Meeting
excerpt: District 8 Councilmember Alyssa Cigarroa pressed city staff Monday over a $425,050 architectural and engineering contract for the Center for the Arts Renovation Project, asking why the agreement referenced an optional planning task that would not be funded.
content:
District 8 Councilmember Alyssa Cigarroa pressed city staff during Monday's City Council meeting over a professional services contract for the Center for the Arts Renovation Project, questioning why the agreement referenced a planning task that was listed as optional and would not be funded.

The item before the council was a contract with JHS Architect of Laredo for architectural and engineering services, in an amount not to exceed $425,050, under RFQ FY26-ENG-20. The funding comes from the 2025 Certificate of Obligation Bond, according to the meeting agenda.

Cigarroa questioned language in the agreement tied to Task 2, a needs assessment, programming and master planning task listed as optional in the firm's proposal at $150,000. She asked staff to explain why the agreement referred to a task that would not be funded.

City staff explained that schematic development would be presented for review before the project moved into its design phase. Cigarroa told staff her question was not being answered, then yielded the floor to District 6 Councilmember Dr. Tyler King.

King asked about the project's overall cost. The firm's proposal puts the assumed estimated construction cost at $3,300,000, with the $425,050 fee covering basic services of $325,050 and $105,000 in supplemental specialty consultant services.

The meeting's minutes were still listed as draft as of early Tuesday, and no final action on the contract was recorded in the city's agenda system at that time.

Source: City of Laredo council agenda, Nov. 16, 2026 (File 26-2110).
